questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain of a stretched wire is called:
questions.explanation: Poisson's ratio is a pure number with no units, because it is the ratio of two strains, and for most materials it lies between 0.2 and 0.4.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 8: Mechanical Properties of Solids

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The root mean square speed of the molecules of an ideal gas of molar mass M at absolute temperature T is:
questions.explanation: Since v(rms) varies as √(T/M), a lighter gas moves faster at the same temperature, which is why hydrogen escapes from the atmosphere more readily than oxygen.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A person suffering from myopia, or short sightedness, can be helped by spectacles using:
options: A converging lens of suitable power
A diverging lens of suitable power
questions.explanation: In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina, so a concave lens diverges the rays slightly before they enter the eye. Hypermetropia needs a convex lens.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following species can act both as a Bronsted acid and as a Bronsted base?
questions.explanation: The bicarbonate ion can donate its proton to give CO₃²⁻ or accept one to give H₂CO₃, so it is amphiprotic. This buffering is what keeps blood pH steady.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Benzoic acid dissolved in benzene gives a van't Hoff factor of about 0.5. This is because benzoic acid molecules:
options: Associate into dimers through hydrogen bonding
questions.explanation: Association halves the number of particles, so i falls below one. Dissociation would instead push i above one, as for NaCl in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Zinc, cadmium and mercury are not regarded as typical transition elements because:
options: Their d orbitals are completely filled in the atom and in all their common oxidation states
They are liquids at room temperature
They have no d electrons at all
questions.explanation: A transition element must have a partly filled d subshell in at least one of its stable oxidation states. With d¹⁰ throughout, these three are colourless and diamagnetic.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 4: The d- and f-Block Elements

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The first stable product formed when acetyl CoA enters the Krebs cycle is:
questions.explanation: Acetyl CoA condenses with oxaloacetic acid to give citric acid, which is why the pathway is also called the citric acid cycle.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 12: Respiration in Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Paul Ehrlich's rivet popper hypothesis compares an ecosystem to an aeroplane and suggests that:
options: The loss of any species is harmless
The loss of each species weakens the ecosystem, and losing key species is far more damaging
Only large animals matter to an ecosystem
Ecosystems cannot be damaged by species loss
questions.explanation: Rivets popped from a wing matter far more than those from a seat, just as the loss of a keystone species harms an ecosystem more than the loss of a rare one.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In the earthworm Pheretima, the clitellum is a glandular thickening of the skin that:
options: Secretes the cocoon in which the eggs are laid
questions.explanation: The clitellum covers segments 14 to 16 and marks the mature worm. Locomotion is helped by the setae, which are absent in these segments.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 7: Structural Organisation in Animals

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The appearance of antibiotic resistant bacteria in a hospital within a few years is best explained as:
options: Natural selection acting on pre-existing variation, observed within our own lifetime
A deliberate change made by the bacteria
questions.explanation: A few bacteria already carry a resistance mutation, the antibiotic kills the rest, and the survivors multiply. This is evolution happening fast enough to observe directly.
